subject: Post-call: Hearthwell security & private deployment qualification
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthwell.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hearthwell security & private deployment qualification

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on qualifying a Private/VPC or on-prem deployment for Hearthwell: 

Call recap (short):
- Goal: support Hearthwell production inference for PHI workloads with isolation options (VPC peering, private VPC, and air-gapped on-prem as a fallback).
- Key constraints: HIPAA obligations, potential EU processing for a subset of telemetry, procurement timelines driven by Q4 budget cycle.

Immediate asks / info we need from your side:
1) SOC 2 status: do you have a current SOC 2 report (Type I/II) or an audit in flight? If in flight, please share expected audit completion date and any letters of attestation you can provide now.
2) Data classification: confirm whether the workloads we would host will include PHI, and if so, which categories (e.g., patient identifiers, structured clinical notes, images).
3) Vendor security questionnaire: if you have an internal questionnaire, please send it over (procurement mentioned they often use a template). We can ingest and respond, and our security team will gap against SOC 2 / HIPAA controls.
4) Network topology: a simple network diagram showing where inference would sit (VPC, subnets, peering/expressroute, firewall zones). I attached a rough draft network-diagram-draft.png and a short proposal (redwood-deploy-proposal.pdf) to illustrate typical patterns — these are placeholders for discussion.

Proposed timeline:
- Please share SOC 2 evidence + questionnaire by EOD Thursday 2028-09-28 if possible.
- We’ll schedule a 30-45min architecture deep-dive the week of Oct 2 to review topology and options (VPC peering vs private deployment vs air-gap).

If helpful, I can loop in our compliance lead (Jordan) and solutions architect (Neha) to review the vendor questionnaire and draft a recommended path with two alternatives (fast: VPC/private tenancy; conservative: air-gapped on-prem), including delta on lead time and estimated cost.

Thanks — attaching: redwood-deploy-proposal.pdf, network-diagram-draft.png.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthwell.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@hearthwell.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Sep 2028 17:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hearthwell security & private deployment qualification

Thanks Stephanie — great summary. A few quick answers inline.

> 1) SOC 2 status:
We completed SOC 2 Type I in 2027 and have a Type II audit scheduled for Q1 2029 (fieldwork Jan 2029). We do not yet have a Type II report; procurement can provide the Type I report and the audit engagement letter.

> 2) Data classification:
Yes — the planned workload will include PHI (structured and unstructured clinical notes). Images are out of scope for the initial phase. We can supply a short inventory of the data elements we expect to send.

> 3) Vendor security questionnaire:
Attaching our standard vendor_security_questionnaire_v1.docx — procurement asked that you review and complete the controls sections.

> 4) Network topology:
We don’t have a finalized topology yet. I reviewed your draft diagram and it looks in line with what we expect. We typically prefer VPC peering with strict egress controls to start, and keep air-gapped on-prem as a longer-term option for highly restricted systems.

Next steps from our side: procurement will review your proposal and I’ll work to get the Type I SOC 2 and the data inventory uploaded to the shared folder you provide. We’re available the week of Oct 2 — Oct 3 or 4 mornings (EST) are preferable for our infra/architecture folks.

-Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Infrastructure & Security
Hearthwell Health
liam.oconnor@hearthwell.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Sep 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Hearthwell follow-up — what we need before arch call

Stephanie / Neha — quick internal note to align before the architecture call: 

Key items we should request from Hearthwell (to be explicit in our Oct 2-4 agenda):
- SOC 2 Type I report (procured now) and the auditor engagement letter for the Type II (dates / scope).
- Full vendor questionnaire completed where possible; highlight any "to be provided" items.
- Data flow diagram (high-level) showing where PHI originates, any ETL layers, storage, and which systems call Redwood.
- Clarify whether PHI will be de-identified before transmission or if we will be receiving raw PHI. This affects encryption & retention controls.
- Expected RTO / RPO targets and latency SLOs for inference.
- Desired deployment model: rank preference (1-3): VPC peering (fastest), private single-tenant (medium), air-gapped on-prem (longest lead).

Technical asks for the arch call so we can prepare:
1) If they pick VPC peering — do they require AWS PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, or simple VPC peering?
2) KMS expectations (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood-managed CMKs).
3) Logging/monitoring access: will they require log forwarding to their SIEM or prefer access via SFTP / secure bucket pull?

Neha — can you draft two deployment options with high-level lead time and cost delta (VPC peering vs air-gapped) and attach to the call invite? I’ll prepare the compliance checklist to compare against their questionnaire.

Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hearthwell.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@hearthwell.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Sep 2028 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hearthwell security & private deployment qualification — next steps and doc request

Liam — thanks for the quick replies and for sharing procurement’s questionnaire. To keep things actionable, can you please provide the following by EOD Thursday 2028-10-04: 

1) SOC evidence: Type I report (as noted) and the auditor engagement letter that confirms the Type II schedule. If you have any interim attestation or SOC readiness assessment, include that too.
2) Completed vendor_security_questionnaire_v1.docx (or indicate which sections are redlines/NA).
3) Short data inventory (list of PHI elements we should expect) and a one-page data flow diagram if you have one. If you don’t, upload whatever topology notes procurement has — we’ll convert into a diagram.
4) Confirm preferred deployment ranking (VPC peering / private single-tenant / air-gapped on-prem).

Proposed call options: Oct 3 at 10:00 AM EST (13:00 PDT) or Oct 4 at 9:00 AM EST — let us know which works and who from your infra/security team will join. We’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (SOC 2 status, data handling, preferred topology, and a review of the questionnaire).

I created a shared folder for document exchange: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GHRxq-Redwood-Hearthwell-Docs — please upload the documents there and paste links in reply. I’ve also created the HubSpot deal record for tracking: hubspot://deals/20483.

Thanks — we’ll review the questionnaire internally once procurement uploads it and come back with clarifying questions before the call.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Redwood Inference
